Physical Go2 camera acceptance for audit1831

Generation does not access a device. All cases begin not_run. Use a reserved
robot and companion with the owner's recorded approval. Perception only: no
locomotion, actuator, posture, power/reset, firmware update or bond commands.
Keep the robot physically stationary according to its owner's safe setup.
Do not treat the generated H264 test as a real firmware recording.

Inventory JSON must contain cli_binary, agent_binary, source_commit, and
consumer_image as a reviewed immutable OCI digest with Python3 and GStreamer
(v4l2src,h264parse,avdec_h264,videoconvert,fdsink). target contains selector,
serial, owner, board, kernel, camera_stable_id. robot contains model="Unitree Go2",
serial, exact firmware version, firmware_record path, wired_interface,
topic="/frontvideostream", resolution=360. records names device_info,
installed_agent, camera_list, kernel_module, ros_interfaces, baseline_apps,
recovery must be actual saved nonempty observations. camera_list is the CLI JSON
array. The firmware record must identify this robot serial and firmware version,
not a screenshot of another robot. Hashes identify inputs, not acceptance.

1. On the reserved companion's owner-controlled local console, record its serial,
   physical wired link to the recorded robot, uname -a, OS and boot identity,
   installed Agent binary digest and MainPID. Independently compare these to
   plan.json and the selected device info. Reject a different robot/companion.
   No SSH, default-device changes, radio reconfiguration, or automatic selection.
   Preserve baseline app states. Check this plan's generated app ID is absent.

2. Require the already owner-installed supported module, without unloading any
   module or stopping any other capture:
     modinfo -F version v4l2loopback
     cat /sys/module/v4l2loopback/version
     v4l2-ctl --device=@NODE@ --all --list-formats-ext
   Require version0.15.4 or a separately qualified compatible0.15+ build, record
   its source and installed module hash. Distro0.12.7 does not qualify. Missing
   module/occupied camera is pending, not permission to change driver state.
   Re-run the exact camera listing and check the stable ROS ID still maps to
   @NODE@, /frontvideostream and the pinned robot-facing interface. Require
   640x360 H264 after the first producer frame. Keep the same Agent PID.

3. Confirm the installed ROS environment provides rclpy and the pinned Unitree
   Go2FrontVideoData message package; save package/source hashes and output of:
     ros2 interface show unitree_go/msg/Go2FrontVideoData
     ros2 topic info /frontvideostream --verbose
   Require exactly one publisher, corroborated against this physically wired
   robot; save its endpoint GUID/type/QoS before and after the capture. DDS camera
   samples are unauthenticated. A second publisher or an unverified interface/RMW
   selection leaves source identity pending. Preserve the reviewed ROS RMW/interface
   configuration with the recording; do not assume ROS_DOMAIN_ID alone selects a
   physical link. These commands only inspect. Run only against this trusted wired robot graph
   with explicit ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0. Do not publish any ROS commands. On the local
   companion console, copy the sealed plan and included go2-record-cdr.py into
   a fresh owned directory, then invoke the exact confirmed robot serial:
     timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=5s 40s env ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0 \
       python3 go2-record-cdr.py --plan plan.json \
       --confirm-robot-serial SERIAL_FROM_PLAN --output raw-recording
   Require exit0 from the recorder; the outer40-second bound is not success.
   The helper subscribes raw to /frontvideostream for30seconds and saves each
   exact CDR sample with length, hash, receipt time and firmware timestamp.
   It refuses non360p/other-layout samples and bounds samples/bytes. An interrupted
   recording, zero/few frames or a different format stays pending. A recorded
   SDK three-JPEG stream does not qualify for the observed H264 firmware case.

4. Keep all robot control unchanged. While recording, an owner presents a fresh
   human-written challenge identifier and moves red, green then blue cards across
   the front camera, repeating every few seconds. Record the presentation times
   and the physical camera/serial being challenged. Do not cover safety sensors
   or alter the robot's environment beyond its approved stationary camera test.
   Concurrently, on the development host run:
     sh @PLAN@/capture-cli.sh
   The35-second deadline and exit124 merely bound capture; they are not success.
   Require a nonempty physical.h264 starting with Annex-B, separate stderr,
   advancing frames and SPS/PPS/IDR followed by non-IDR slices. Independently decode:
     ffmpeg -v error -f h264 -i @PLAN@/physical.h264 -f null -
     ffprobe -v error -select_streams v:0 -show_entries stream=codec_name,width,height \
       -show_entries frame=key_frame,pict_type,best_effort_timestamp_time -of json @PLAN@/physical.h264
   Save both exit codes and reports; require H264640x360 and at least30 decoded
   frames. Review the video against the exact challenge/time notes. Codec metadata,
   growing bytes, or successful discovery alone cannot pass.

5. Stop only this plan's bounded CLI capture before starting its container, to
   avoid conflating simultaneous capture negotiation with container delivery.
   Recheck the same stable camera ID and node. Validate the generated consumer
   project with the pinned CLI, then run its exact deploy_owned_consumer command.
   This creates only the unique app listed in plan.json, with the parameterless
   camera entitlement. It decodes60 kernel H264 buffers using an independent
   decoder, without a ROS or robot-control publisher. Present the same timed
   three-color challenge during this capture. Detached deploy is not acceptance:
   fetch exact app logs and require normal exit0, the matching nonce/node,
   H264640x360, exactly60 decoded frames, at least20 distinct frame hashes, and
   center RGB means consistent with the owner's timed color challenge. Require
   actual runtime label sh.wendy/entitlement.camera to be nonempty via the
   owner-controlled local companion containerd inspection, with exact app ID.
   Do not inspect or modify another container. A blank label, only a host stream,
   a node that exists but cannot deliver frames, forced timeout, or stale frame
   sequence fails container acceptance. Save app state and its complete log.

6. Copy the raw-recording directory and physical.h264 to the review artifact store
   outside Git, retaining per-sample hashes, pinned firmware/serial/source records
   and challenge notes. Do not commit images/videos or substitute generated frames.
   Recorded service replay remains pending until this exact archived corpus is
   replayed through the production CDR parser/writer/service and independently
   decoded with matching frame content. The automated generated-video gate does
   not consume this archive and must not be used to claim recorded replay passed.

7. Run only remove_owned_consumer for this exact generated app ID. It does not
   delete volumes or image caches. Verify its absence and compare baseline app
   states, Agent PID, camera identity and owner normal read-only camera probe.
   Do not remove production containers, recordings or ROS camera registry entries.
   Preserve incomplete/failing evidence; module and robot state stay owner-managed.
   A human may mark each completed case passed only with its cited evidence.
